newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower; LME stocks up, spreads in.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower; LME stocks up, spreads in.

text.p: COMEX copper prices ended lower largely on trade selling as London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks continued their trend upward as the LME backwardation narrowed.
The LME warehouse stockpile increased another 5,000 tonnes to 200,950 tonnes, a new four-month high, while the benchmark cash-to-three-month backwardation narrowed to $57/$67.
The active COMEX September contract settled at 105.60 cents a pound, down 1.25 cents from Tuesday, while the spot month fell 2.00 cents to 107.90 cents.
"The LME stocks set the tone for the market early," said James Quinn, commodity commentator for A.G. Edwards & Co. "We were lower right out of the box.
"There's some question as to how low the prices have to fall before we see some buying from the Asian sector," he added.

Physical traders insist that Asian demand is weak. "Asia is dead," one dealer quipped. "All of the material going into Singapore goes to show that there's little need for copper in that part of the world."
LME Singapore stocks increased another 925 tonnes in Wednesday's report and has increased by 29,575 tonnes to 51,225 tonnes in the last 12 trading days.
The last time LME warehouse stocks were at the current levels was March 17. At that time the September price was 103.70 cents a pound.
Near-term support was pegged at 103.00 cents in the September contract. "But I wouldn't expect to the funds get spooked until 101.00 cents," Edwards' Quinn said.
